body: Steering with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offers a lightweight inference-time path for adapting the behavior of large language models without retraining. By exposing sparse and interpretable features, SAE steering provides a promising interface for safety control that guides harmful continuations toward refusal. However, we observe that complex wrappers can still undermine existing SAE steering methods on harmful prompts. To evaluate this failure mode systematically, we construct Generalized Undercover Instruction Safety Evaluation (GUISE), a dataset of harmful prompts with complex wrappers. Existing single direction SAE steering methods do not reliably produce refusals on harmful prompts, suggesting that refusal enhancement alone can be too weak when the harmful continuation path remains active. This motivates us to propose Refusal-Enhanced INhibitory Steering (REINS), which suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features in the same SAE feature space. Experiments on GUISE and other datasets show that prior methods either intervene too weakly or achieve only apparent safety through collapse, while REINS substantially reduces harmful responses, markedly improves safe refusals and largely preserves general capabilities.
summaryZh: 稀疏自编码器（SAE）为大模型提供了轻量级的推理期行为适配路径，但复杂的提示词包装常使其失效。本文提出Generalized Undercover Instruction Safety Evaluation（GUISE）数据集用以评估该失效模式，并进一步引入Refusal-Enhanced INhibitory Steering（REINS）方法。REINS通过在同一SAE特征空间中抑制有害连续特征并增强安全拒绝特征，大幅降低了有害响应，改善了安全拒绝率且基本保留了模型的通用能力。

aiReview.reasonZh: 提出了REINS方法，结合稀疏自编码器特征在同一空间中抑制有害续写并增强安全拒绝机制，有效提升了大模型推理时的安全控制能力。

glossary.explanationZh: 稀疏自编码器，用于将大模型内部激活分解为稀疏且可解释特征的技术。
一种包含复杂包装的有害提示词数据集，用于系统评估安全对齐失效模式。
一种通过抑制有害特征并增强拒绝特征来提升安全控制的推理期干预方法。
推理期，指在模型生成输出时进行计算或干预的阶段，无需重新训练。
